hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $x e^x$: product rule gives $1 \cdot e^x + x \cdot e^x$. Same shape here, with $\ln x$ and its derivative $\frac{1}{x}$.
$f'(x) = 1 \cdot \ln x + x \cdot \frac{1}{x} = \ln x + 1$. Now use $\ln e = 1$.

explanation: Product rule with $u = x$ and $v = \ln x$: $f'(x) = u'v + uv' = \ln x + x \cdot \frac{1}{x}$.
The second term simplifies to $1$, so $f'(x) = \ln x + 1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Common trap
steps: Forgetting the product rule gives $f'(x) = \frac{1}{x}$, which at $x = e$ is about $0.37$ — much too small.
The product rule answer $2$ is the one the numbers back up.
